utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Stanojevic. As I was preparing for my cross-examination, we looked at yesterday's testimony and we decided to clarify just a few things with the witness, so I believe that my cross-examination will last much shorter than I announced yesterday. Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kindly help us clarify a few issues. Yesterday when you were talking about your arrival in Kravica, you mentioned a machine that had already been there. To the Prosecutor's question, you described that machine. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were shown a photo which should reflect the appearance of that machine and you said yes, that is the machine with a scoop. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that that machine did not belong to the engineers company of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't belong to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to yourself, on the day when you were in Kravica and Glogova, was there anybody else there from the engineers company of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was the only one there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ostoja. And I wanted to clarify one more thing. Yesterday you mentioned the name of Rajko Djokic.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were also there with you [as interpreted] in Bratunac on the 15th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on Sunday morning that was -- no, it was on Saturday. Yes, he was with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, would you please stop for a while. It seems that my monitor has something wrong. The laptop is okay, but the monitor is something wrong. I'm just afraid that we missed some transcript in the monitor. Well, should we wait for the technicians to check our monitor or should we proceed, because you know, we have the laptop here and the transcript is in the laptop. Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your Honour, our laptop on this computer is not working. It still just says 5th of December, open session, and nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. So I'm afraid that we have to wait for a minute. But it seems to me that everything is okay. So shall we proceed while the technician will come into the courtroom to look at that laptop of the Defence team. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Your Honour. Once again, this cross-examination is not going to take a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to that day. We were talking about Rajko Djokic and you confirmed to me that he was in Bratunac on that day and that he stayed with you in Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened? Can you help us and tell us where he was. Where did he stay when you were in Kravica and in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that he was in the municipality. Where he was on that day, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that he also was not either in Kravica or in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Djokic; no, he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that Rajko Djokic, captain first class, at the beginning of the war was a commander of a battalion, and then, because of his advanced age, he was transferred to the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that he worked in the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that he was captain first class and reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a reserve officer. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And one more thing, please. Am I right in saying that in Glogova, you did not see anybody from the engineers company, none of their members or machines?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anybody. There were just two workers who worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to take the opportunity to have -- of having you here to ask you how long have you known Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Dragan Jokic on the 23rd of June, 1992, when I joined the Serbian army. That was on the 23rd of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe Dragan Jokic as a person, as an officer.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't complain. He was a good man. He was a good officer. He was good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he make any profits during the war, or was he the person who shared the destiny of his people and his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely as you put it. He hasn't made any profit. He has exactly the things that he started with. He has nothing more than he had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that his soul was pure during the war and after the war?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any redirect, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any documents to tender through this witness. Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. There are two documents, and they are the two diagrams that were referred to by the witness, P669 and P670.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objections to the admission of these two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So these two exhibits are admitted into the evidence. I guess there is no evidence to tender through this witness by the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I guess there is no witness on the list for this week.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That completes the witnesses for this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, are there any procedural matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing I can think of, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing in particular, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I was going to try to handle this informally, Your Honour, but since we have a few moments, I would like to mention that, as far as I remember, the Trial Chamber did order that five days after the last intercept witness our final reply to the Prosecution's motion to admit intercept evidence would be due. Of course, five days after that will fall right in the middle of the Christmas holiday. I was hoping that the Trial Chamber would be home enjoying their family during this break, and therefore would not be forced to read any documents from this trial at that point. So I was going to ask that since it does fall right at Christmas, maybe the Court would entertain allowing this to be filed after the first week in January. But Judge Liu did indicate that he will not be home with his family, so I understand he'll be here reading everything I write. But that's my request is if we could just wait until after the Christmas holiday since the whole Tribunal, as far as I understand, will be closed down the 19th of December, afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. McCloskey, could you please indicate to us how many intercepts are still not introduced and is going to be introduced before the Christmas break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the remaining intercept witness is a completely different sort of intercept than the Court has already seen. As you know, the -- this is what we refer to as the tactical intercepts. The person that had responsibility for taking the tactical intercepts is -- will be here, and he has a collection of those tactical intercepts. They're very rough jotted notes. You've seen them, I'm sure you remember, Mr. Obrenovic talking about the tactical intercepts where the two engineers were mentioned. That's what this has to do with. Because it has to do with Mr. Obrenovic and these two engineers, one of whom we have actually seen testify, we thought it was important to give you the full picture and let you hear about these tactical intercepts. So this one person will testify about those intercept collection and that intercept in particular. But it's a much -- these are -- when we say tactical, as you may have seen from the witness summary, these are soldiers in the woods with smaller radios, collecting different sorts of radio communications than the fellows on the big mountaintops. So it's really apples and oranges in terms of intercepts, but it's a small collection that we've already heard about before, and I don't anticipate him being on the stand for too long, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But some of those intercepts are also important to the Defence case, as I understand, and it may show the custody or the techniques or ways to obtain those intercepts. And, Ms. Sinatra, I think we have gone through the -- if I say the most essential intercept witnesses already, and during which the Prosecution provided a lot of intercepts. And during that period you raised a lot of objections. And after hearing your objections as well as the testimony of those witnesses, we gave you five days to provide us with further objections if you have. We have to deal with those documents section by section, or group by group, and it is our intention to make a ruling concerning of the intercepts before the winter recess so that the parties would have a very clear picture of where they are standing. If some intercepts are not admitted into the evidence, the Prosecution still has the opportunity before their case closes to call more witnesses to testify on that particular intercept. So, Ms. Sinatra, if you have any objections to those group of intercepts, we would like to have your written submissions as soon as possible so that we could render a decision on that. As for the forthcoming intercept witnesses and intercepts, you may - you may - file your objections if there is any before the resuming of this case next year. Is that understandable?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I just want to make it clear so that I understand. What you're saying is that I have not filed a reply to the response of the Prosecution's response to our objections to the intercepts. I have a very short piece. I'm not quite sure when the date is due for our reply, but you're giving us until the resumption of the trial proceedings in January to finalise our objections? Is that my understanding of the Trial Chamber's decision?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. I mean that we have to deal with those intercepts group by group. I think for the first group, it's about the live testimony of some witnesses here concerning with those intercepts. If you did not file your reply, I hope you could file it as soon as possible, because I believe that we have to make a decision before the winter recess. As for the forthcoming intercepts, you may file it at the resuming of this trial in January.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: So, Your Honour, could I have a rock-bottom deadline to file my reply. Could that be at least the 17th or 18th of December? Would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, you have to give us some time to read your reply. I give you another week.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Another week from today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: From today, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I just wanted to make it clear so I wasn't missing a deadline. Okay, thank you. I'll try to take care of it, and a famous Chinese proverb: When in Rome, do as the Romans do, so I promise I'll take care of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have a similar proverb, but I don't know whether this is Chinese or English. Well, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Trial Chamber? I see none. So the hearing is adjourned. We'll resume next week in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 12.22 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of December, 2003, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
